title_en: Why Koreans press this button non-stop #shorts
description_en: Every Korean elevator has a close button, and almost nobody waits for the doors. The reason is one word: ppalli-ppalli. Learn 빨리빨리, 배달 (delivery) and 닫힘 (close). Stock footage: Pexels (free license)
hook_en: Why do Koreans spam this button?
hook_vi: Vì sao người Hàn bấm nút này liên tục?
hook_id: Kenapa orang Korea tekan tombol ini terus?
hook_voice: Why do Koreans spam this button?

scenes.voice: Koreans have a name for it: ppalli-ppalli. Faster, faster. Speed is the default.

scenes.vi: Giao hàng lúc 2 giờ sáng. Trong 20 phút.
scenes.id: Antar pesanan jam 2 pagi. Dalam 20 menit.
scenes.voice: Delivery is baedal. At two in the morning, it still takes twenty minutes.

scenes.en: The close button. Pressed ten times.
scenes.vi: Nút đóng cửa. Bấm mười lần.
scenes.voice: So in the elevator: dachim. The close button, pressed ten times before the doors move. Not rude. Just ppalli-ppalli.

cta.en: Slow is okay too. Do you press it too? 👇
cta.vi: Chậm lại cũng được. Bạn cũng bấm nút đó chứ? 👇
cta.id: Pelan-pelan juga boleh. Kamu juga menekannya? 👇
cta.voice: And when you want to slow down: cheoncheonhi haedo dwaeyo. So, do you press it too?
